expected_solc_divergence.reason: solc reads the components past the third as a second comparator, so it takes '0.8.36.0' as '0.8.36' followed by '0', and the latter holds for any version whose major is '0' — which makes solc accept the pragma on '0.8.36' alone. Slang keeps the literal as the four-component version it is, which names no release, so it admits nothing on any version. On '0.8.37' solc reads the same literal as '0.8.36' followed by '0', which no longer matches the compiler running it, so both reject it and the divergence ends.
